title: Firebase Data Connect Production Design Review

questions.question: Which three contracts make up a deployed Firebase Data Connect service?
options: A browser cache, a WebSocket server, and a document database
The PostgreSQL SQL schema, the Data Connect application schema, and deployed connectors
Only a GraphQL schema and Firebase Hosting
A generated SDK, a CDN, and Security Rules
questions.explanation: PostgreSQL remains the data source of truth, the application schema maps the model exposed to Data Connect, and connectors define the operations clients may call.

questions.question: Why can a generated SDK be safer than letting a web client submit arbitrary GraphQL text?
options: The SDK makes every query free
The SDK calls named, deployed connector operations with generated variable and result types
The SDK bypasses authorization directives
The SDK stores PostgreSQL rows in the browser
questions.explanation: The client contract is generated from predefined connector operations. Selection sets, authorization, and operation shape are reviewed and deployed server-side.

questions.question: A ListMyFavorites operation uses @auth(level: USER) but filters with a userId supplied by the client. What is the main problem?
options: The query cannot use PostgreSQL indexes
Authentication does not prove that the supplied userId belongs to the caller
The generated SDK cannot represent strings
Firebase Authentication cannot issue user IDs
questions.explanation: USER proves that a non-anonymous user signed in. Ownership should be derived or filtered with the server-evaluated auth.uid, not trusted from a client argument.

questions.question: What happens when a client-accessible connector operation omits @auth?
options: It becomes PUBLIC
It inherits Cloud SQL IAM from the browser
It defaults to NO_ACCESS and cannot be executed by a client
It skips Firebase Authentication but enforces ownership
questions.explanation: Operations default to NO_ACCESS when @auth is absent. Privileged Admin SDK execution is a separate server-side boundary.

questions.question: Which migration mode is the safer starting point for a Cloud SQL database that already contains production data outside the application schema?
options: STRICT, because it drops every unused object
COMPATIBLE, because optional schema, table, and column drops are not applied
Force deploy, because it disables PostgreSQL constraints
No migration, because connectors update the SQL schema automatically at runtime
questions.explanation: Compatible mode applies changes required by the application schema while leaving unrelated database objects in place. Destructive changes still need a deliberate plan.

questions.question: Why should removing a connector field be separated into staged releases?
options: Old generated clients may still depend on that field
PostgreSQL cannot store nullable fields
Data Connect connectors are evaluated only in the browser
A generated SDK never changes
questions.explanation: First stop selecting the field where compatible, ship regenerated SDKs and clients, then remove the schema field in a later migration after old clients are retired.

questions.question: Which cost and health boundaries must be monitored separately?
options: Only generated TypeScript bundle size
Data Connect operations and egress, plus Cloud SQL compute, storage, availability, and query health
Only the count of GraphQL type definitions
Only Firebase Authentication users
questions.explanation: Data Connect service usage and the backing Cloud SQL instance are separate billable and operational components. A healthy API layer does not prove that PostgreSQL capacity or backups are healthy.
